title: Macroscopic Quantum Interference of the Center-of-Mass Motion of Levitated Superconducting Microparticles enabled by Magnetic Higher-Order Traps
authors: Jaume Cunill-Subiranas, Fabian Resare, Suocheng Zhao, Sofia Qvarfort, A. Metelmann, Carles Navau, Witlef Wieczorek
abstract: We show how magnetostatic higher-order multipole traps can be used to generate macroscopic quantum interference of the motion of levitated superconducting microparticles. An appropriate combination of multipolar magnetic fields offers great versatility in constructing various trap potentials, including anharmonic trap potentials such as Duffing or double-well types. Crucially, the anharmonic trap potentials realize a nonlinearity on the order of hundred times the zero-point motion, i.e., on a length scale below nanometers. These anharmonic potentials allow for the generation of quantum features of the center-of-mass motion of a magnetically levitated superconducting microparticle. Importantly, they can be easily generated with a static arrangement of coils, requiring only that the current running through them is tunable. We propose protocols exploiting the versatility of the magnetic trap landscape to generate non-Gaussian motional states. We solve the dynamics of the center-of-mass motion of the particle in phase space and analyze its parameter dependence. Furthermore, we give a recipe to distinguish classical from quantum behavior in a statistically meaningful way through measurement of the position of the particle. Our results open a path to accessing the quantum regime of the center-of-mass motion of objects with masses larger than picogram, i.e., $10^{13}$ atomic mass units. This will enable fundamental physics experiments for studying the transition between quantum and classical behavior, exploring the intersection between quantum physics and gravity as well as probing of certain types of dark matter.
summary: The paper details the use of advanced magnetic traps, generated by higher-order multipoles, to confine levitated superconducting microparticles. This confinement creates anharmonic potentials necessary for inducing nonclassical quantum motion in the particle's center-of-mass. The research paves the way for fundamental experiments testing the boundary between classical and quantum mechanics using massive mechanical oscillators.
main_problem: The central goal is generating and observing macroscopic quantum interference effects in the center-of-mass motion of levitated superconducting microparticles.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that using higher-order multipole magnetic traps allows for the creation of anharmonic potentials capable of realizing non-Gaussian motional states, opening a path to study the quantum-to-classical transition with massive objects.
method: The analysis involves solving the dynamics of the center-of-mass motion in phase space, utilizing Wigner function representations and analyzing specific nonlinear potential forms like Duffing or double-well potentials.
model_or_system: The system is a superconducting microparticle levitated and trapped by static magnetic fields generated via higher-order multipole coils. The dynamics are governed by the particle's interaction with an anharmonic potential $U(r)$ derived from the applied field $\mathbf{B}_a$.
key_observables: Non-Gaussian motional states, measurement of particle position to distinguish classical vs. quantum behavior.
important_parameters: The nonlinearity scale is set below nanometers (hundred times the zero-point motion); trap potentials are defined by magnetic field coefficients ($b_1, b_2, b_3$).
main_assumptions: It is assumed that the superconducting particle remains in a state where its dynamics can be effectively modeled by these anharmonic potentials, and that rapid switching of fields is possible.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates various magnetic traps (harmonic/anharmonic) generated by coil configurations. Figure 2 shows classical trajectory solutions for different nonlinear potential types (DP, DWP).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical platform and the role of higher-order traps in creating anharmonic potentials. It then analyzes the resulting dynamics using phase space methods, deriving specific protocols to generate nonclassical states before concluding with implications for fundamental physics tests.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum mechanics (quantum interference, non-Gaussian states) with macroscopic mechanical systems and superconducting materials, making it highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum sensing in AMO physics.
